The upstream normalized Code Enforcement Officer record was incorrectly tagged as police; this validation corrects the candidate interpretation from the verbatim source line but does not overwrite the raw upstream record. The negative $0.91/hour documentary difference pertains only to these two specifically listed schedule values and must not be generalized to police and non-safety employees in Canastota. This is bounded local documentary evidence, not a final wage-gap estimate, and is not nationally representative. Substantive/manual validation of occupational and schedule-position comparability is required before analytic use beyond a qualified supporting example.

safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.assertion: Safety-position wages grow faster than non-safety-position wages.
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.local_comparison_support: partial: 21 supporting or conditional local documentary comparison records; no global estimator
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.mechanism_support: pass: 37,369 mechanism records and 1,682 quant-qual links support institutional wage-pressure channels
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.national_readiness_support: partial: 35,623 readiness strata describe coverage and blockers, not national outcomes
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.non_base_compensation_support: partial but extensive: 8,422 evidence units; total-compensation harmonization remains incomplete
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.recommended_bounded_wording: The corpus supports a bounded causal-mechanism interpretation: safety compensation appears especially exposed to a reinforcing bundle of bargaining, impasse resolution, step progression, non-base compensation, recruitment/retention pressure, comparability, and retroactive implementation. These institutions can raise floors, schedule growth, protect add-ons, strengthen leverage, and make delayed increases payable. Non-safety units also receive several of these mechanisms, so the evidence supports the direction of the safety wage-pressure story more strongly than a universal safety-only mechanism or a clean global wage-gap estimate.
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.same_side_growth_support: partial: 1,945 growth evidence units, including claim-ready/supporting records with heterogeneous periods and structures
strongest_countervailing_or_limiting_evi: The 21 local comparison records are supporting or conditional examples, not a scalable wage-gap estimator.
Mechanism evidence counts are coded spans and can repeat within sources.
Non-safety units also receive bargaining, COLA, step, and pay-plan mechanisms.
Pay basis, period, and role comparability remain incomplete in national strata.
Documented institutional channels do not identify counterfactual wage outcomes.
Budget and adoption mechanisms can constrain or delay as well as increase compensation.
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.what_evidence_would_upgrade_this_asserti: A repeated city-by-cycle contract panel with comparable safety/non-safety roles, harmonized total compensation, validated implementation dates, external controls, and credible identifying variation.
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.why_causal_estimate_is_not_ready: The documentary corpus identifies mechanisms and plausible direction but supplies no validated counterfactual design, regression, shock, or treatment-effect estimate.
safety_wage_growth_assertion_assessment.why_global_wage_gap_estimate_is_not_read: The corpus lacks sufficient clean, repeated, same-city same-cycle cross-side comparisons with compatible pay basis, periods, and roles.

same_side_evidence_boundary: Supports bounded statements about named units, structures, and periods without supplying a cross-side wage gap.
